response.text:
For several days after leaving Nantucket, nothing above hatches was seen of Captain Ahab. The mates regularly relieved each other; yet, ever and anon, they came from the cabin with sudden, peremptory orders: they but commanded vicariously. Their supreme lord and dictator was there, unseen in the now sacred retreat.

My vague disquiet touching the unknown captain, heightened by Elijah’s diabolical incoherences, grew at sea to perturbation; yet the mates allayed misgivings. Running south, winter bit us less and less; and on one of those grey, gloomy mornings of the transition, when with a fair wind the ship was rushing through the water with a vindictive sort of leaping and melancholy rapidity, I mounted to the deck—foreboding shivers—and reality outran apprehension: Captain Ahab stood upon his quarter-deck.

No common illness marked him. He looked like a man cut away from the stake when the fire has wasted all the limbs without consuming them; his high, broad form seemed solid bronze, shaped in an unalterable mould, like Cellini’s Perseus. Threading from among his grey hairs, and down one side of his scorched face and neck, disappeared in his clothing, a slender, livid, rod-like mark—as when upper lightning peels and grooves a lofty trunk, leaving it greenly alive but branded. Whether birth-mark or the scar of some desperate wound, no one could say. Then, too, the barbaric white leg upon which he partly stood—the ivory fashioned from the polished jaw-bone of a sperm whale. He steadied it in an auger-hole bored near the mizzen shrouds; one arm held a shroud; his face fixed straight out beyond the ever-pitching prow. In that fearless forward dedication of glance was an infinity of firmest fortitude; in his face, a crucifixion; in all the nameless regal overbearing dignity of some mighty woe. He spoke not; nor did the officers address him; yet in their minutest gestures, they owned the uneasy consciousness of a troubled master-eye.

Ere long he withdrew; but thereafter he was daily visible—at his pivot-hole, upon an ivory stool, or pacing the deck. As the sky grew less gloomy he grew less recluse. For a time, he seemed as unnecessary as another mast; the Pequod was but making a passage; the mates sufficed, and there was little, out of himself, to employ him; and thus nothing chased away, for that interval, the clouds that, layer upon layer, were piled upon his brow, as ever all clouds choose the loftiest peaks to pile themselves upon. Nevertheless, the warm, warbling persuasiveness of the holiday weather gradually charmed him a little from his mood; more than once he put forth the faint blossom of a look which, in any other man, would have soon flowered out in a smile.
